summary: Round 11. Every element round 10 and the test review prescribed is present and TRUE at these bytes: 'and the only copy of it' is gone from scripts/check-io-seam.sh:7; M0.112 now records that AGENTS.md, code-structure.md and the M0.107 cell each hold the count and all twelve names, and I re-measured all three as accurate (twelve names, same twelve as PACKAGES, BAN_ENTRIES 28); the two new IoSeamShapeTest cases each genuinely die under the mutation they claim, because their fixtures contain no unmutated alternative -- the pkg-split fixture splits BOTH occurrences of java.nio.file and the lowercase-receiver fixture holds no capitalised receiver before a .now(). I re-measured the numeric claims the earlier rounds established and none moved: 53 non-exempt files name java.io./java.util.zip., exactly eight java.io types are used (ByteArrayInputStream, ByteArrayOutputStream, Closeable, FilterInputStream, IOException, InputStream, OutputStream, UncheckedIOException), 11 src/main files match the implements pattern against binstore-backends' 2. But the delta BROKE the thing round 10 explicitly verified as intact: the backlog edit inserted blank lines INSIDE the task table, which ends a GFM table, so 75 rows -- M0.108 through the last M5 row, including the M0.112 row this commit exists to add -- no longer render as table rows at all. That is M0.109's own defect class, one shape further on, introduced by the edit that records it. No object-store request is added or changed: the gate is a static text scan over source files at commit time and issues nothing at runtime, so nothing here scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.title: the backlog edit inserted blank lines inside the task table; 75 rows from M0.108 down, including the new M0.112 row, fall out of the table
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED at the staged bytes against HEAD. `git show :docs/internal/product/backlog.md | cat -A` shows EMPTY lines at 46, 47 (after the M0.107 row), 50 (after M0.109) and 54, 55 (after M0.112). `git diff --cached -U0` attributes all five to this commit: the hunks are `@@ -45 +45,3 @@` (the M0.107 row plus two blank lines), `@@ -47 +49,2 @@` (M0.109 plus one) and `@@ -49,0 +53,3 @@` (M0.112 plus two). In HEAD that table runs unbroken: `git show HEAD:docs/internal/product/backlog.md | awk 'NR>=27{if($0 ~ /^\|[- ]*\|/){print "delimiter",NR;exit} if($0=="")print "blank",NR}'` prints its first blank at 119, i.e. the end of the table. GFM ends a table at the first blank line, and the lines after it start no new table because no header+delimiter pair follows -- the next delimiter row is at line 129. Consequence a reader suffers: the table now stops at M0.107, and the 75 rows between line 48 and line 127 (M0.108, M0.109, M0.110, M0.111, M0.112 and every M5.37+ row) render as one paragraph of literal text with visible pipes, with no ID, Serves or State column. The row this commit adds to record M0.107's deferred defects -- M0.112 -- is among them, so the verdict-prescribed record is present in the bytes and invisible in the rendered backlog, which is precisely the failure M0.109 was opened for ('the word `done` did not appear in the row at all'). Round 10's verified_from_previous_round says 'no orphan non-pipe line sits inside any table, so the M0.109 defect shapes are absent'; that is no longer true. No gate sees it: check-backlog-table.sh does not exist, check-commit-msg.sh greps the row line-wise so it still finds M0.107, and check-links.sh does not parse tables. FIX, AND IT IS A DELETION OF WHITESPACE, NOT PROSE: remove the five empty lines at 46, 47, 50, 54 and 55 so the rows are contiguous again; the cells themselves are correct -- each of M0.107, M0.109 and M0.112 has exactly 4 unescaped-pipe cells against the 4-column header and ends with a pipe. Touch no text while doing it.

findings.title: the M0.107 cell's 'one class of forty' contradicts the javadoc added in the same commit, which says 'one class of a hundred'; measured 101
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: `git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java' | grep -vc '^binstore-backends/'` prints 101. The M0.107 Task cell still reads 'a one-off test here would cover one class of forty and make the absence look closed' while buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/IoSeamGateTest.java:20 makes the identical argument as 'covers one class of a hundred'. Two documents in one commit give two denominators for one measurement and one of them is wrong by 2.5x. This is round 10's R10-2 unchanged and unrecorded -- M0.112 took four of round 9's five minors and dropped this one, so it is now in no row and in no fix. NOT BLOCKING, for the same reason round 10 gave: the argument holds at 40, 101 or 1000, and the number is not marked MEASURED. If R11-1 is being fixed anyway the cell is not being retyped, so the cheaper resolution is one clause on M0.112 naming the stale denominator, or leave it and let this verdict be the record.

findings.title: IoSeamLexerTest's javadoc describes a two-way split that the second split invalidated: four shape cases remain in IoSeamGateTest and the enumeration omits the coverage tables
findings.failure_scenario: Read at the staged bytes. The javadoc says 'every case here is about io_seam_scan.code_only ... and every case left behind is about what the gate then DOES with them -- its scope, its one exemption, its reporting and its error paths.' That sentence was true of a two-file split and is not true of the three-file one this commit lands. IoSeamGateTest still holds takingAClockAsASeamParameterIsACCEPTED:272, handlingAnInputStreamIsACCEPTEDWhileOPENINGOneIsNot:334, theBYTETypesInABannedPackageAreACCEPTEDWhileItsFILETypesAreNot:475 and GETTINGTheRuntimeIsACCEPTEDWhileEXECUTINGThroughItIsNot:504, all four of which ask whether a given SPELLING is the banned thing -- IoSeamShapeTest's own stated question, and the last of them is the Runtime.getRuntime()/.exec( pair, a shape distinction with nothing to do with scope, the exemption, reporting or error paths. The enumeration also drops the coverage tables (everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED:164, theSuccessLineCountsTheConstructsTheListACTUALLYHolds:362), which the M0.107 State cell does list among what IoSeamGateTest holds, so the two descriptions of the same split disagree. Consequence: a maintainer adding a case about an accepted spelling reads this javadoc, believes shape cases all live in IoSeamShapeTest, and either adds a duplicate there or moves the four -- a rename round on a suite that is already green. The cheap fix is deleting the four-item enumeration and stopping at 'what the gate then DOES with them'; do not add a fifth item, because the boundary is genuinely fuzzy and prose asserting it is sharp is what made this task eleven rounds.

verified_from_previous_round: R10-1 FIXED, and by the prescribed deletion rather than a rewrite: scripts/check-io-seam.sh:7 now reads "`io_seam_scan.py`'s `PACKAGES` is the list -- NO COUNT AND NO ENUMERATION APPEARS HERE". The header names java.io, java.util.zip, java.util.jar, java.sql and javax.sql as EXAMPLES in later paragraphs, none of them presented as the list, so the 'no enumeration' claim stands and no number in the header moves when PACKAGES grows.

The M0.112 clause is TRUE and complete at three: AGENTS.md:151-155, docs/internal/standards/code-structure.md:20-25 and the M0.107 State cell each carry the count 'twelve' and all twelve names, and each enumeration matches PACKAGES exactly (java.nio.file, java.nio.channels, java.io, java.util.zip, java.util.jar, java.util.prefs, java.util.logging, java.sql, javax.sql, javax.naming, java.net, javax.net). IoSeamGateTest also holds the names but is checked against the list by everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED, which is why excluding it from the three is right.

The two new cases are SOLE-KILLER-shaped and I checked the property their claim rests on rather than the claim. IoSeamShapeTest.aPACKAGENameSplitAcrossLinesIsSTILLCounted:92 writes 'java.nio\n        .file.Files.readAllBytes(java.nio\n        .file.Path.of("/x"))' -- BOTH qualified names are split, so no unmutated java.nio.file remains for a whitespace-blind _package to match, which is exactly the first-draft defect the javadoc says was measured and fixed. IoSeamShapeTest.aLOWERCASEReceiverIsAValueAndItsNowAccessorIsACCEPTED:117 holds 'window.now()' with the only capitalised token, Window, followed by a space and an identifier rather than a dot, so the unmutated r'\b[A-Z][\w$]*\s*\.\s*now\s*\(\s*\)' cannot match and the widened [A-Za-z_$] head must.

Numbers re-measured at these bytes, none stale: 53 non-exempt src/main files name java.io. or java.util.zip.; exactly eight java.io types appear in non-exempt src/main and all eight are in ALLOWED; 11 src/main files match implements .*(BinStore|Sequencer|SubscriptionTransport|Membership|Clock) against binstore-backends' 2 (LocalFsBinStore, MemoryBinStore), which is the 'FIVE TIMES WIDER' claim in check-io-seam.sh, code-structure.md and IoSeamGateTest's javadoc; PACKAGES 12 + BANNED 16 = 28 ban entries, which is what the success line prints and what the M0.107 cell's 'TWELVE of the twenty-eight' relies on.

The third test-review finding (dropping _shape's trailing word boundary, under which this.execute(stmt) is refused) is recorded as M0.112's sixth item with the right direction stated (false refusal, self-announcing) and the right grouping (same family as (a)). Not fixed here, as advised.

Cell shape of the three edited rows is correct: M0.107, M0.109 and M0.112 each split into 4 cells against the 4-column header and each ends with a trailing pipe. The M0.109 shapes that are ABSENT are the ones the row names; the one it does not name -- a blank line between rows -- is R11-1.
